title: Polyload congestion runbook (scratch)
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
- Goal: probe how the serving runtime behaves when two semantically different request classes (short embeddings + long-context generation) are present simultaneously on the same GPU host pool. We call this scenario 'polyload' — multiple load shapes contending for shared resources (KV cache, device memory, batching lanes).
- Quick finding (headline): with a 30/70 mix (30% embeddings, 70% generation) we see median latency for gen paths rise modestly, but p95/p99 inflate disproportionately due to KV-cache churn and intermittent OOM-driven host swaps. Embedding latency also shows bimodality when gen concurrency spikes.

Environment & baseline:
- Model variants: gen: redwood-gpt-4o-8k (quantized int8), embed: redwood-embed-lite-v1 (fp16).
- Hardware: single A100-40GB (driver 525.116), container image: rwinference/serving:canary-2026-02.
- Serving config: continuous batching enabled; batching window = 12ms; max_batch_tokens = 8192; kv_cache_shard = enabled; preemption_policy = soft-priority (background lanes preemptible).
- Baseline (gen-only): steady-state QPS 80 gen req/s; median gen lat = 48ms/token, p95 ~ 240ms, p99 ~ 560ms.

Polyload experiment matrix (sweep highlights):
- Mix ratios tested: 0/100, 10/90, 30/70, 50/50, 70/30, 90/10 (embed/gen).
- Gen context lengths: 512, 2048, 4096 tokens.
- Embed batch sizes: 1, 8, 32 (embeds are small but GPU memory spikes when batched).
- Concurrent clients: synthetic Poisson arrival vs real-client replay (captured prod trace day-2026-01-14).

Representative run (30/70, gen ctx=2048, embed batch=8, Poisson arrivals):
- Gen throughput target: 60 qps; embed QPS: 25 qps.
- Observed: mean gen latency increased 12% over baseline; p95 increased from 240ms -> 420ms; p99 jumped from 560ms -> 1.8s. Embedding median latency stayed <40ms, but a second mode appears around 700-900ms aligning with host preemption events.
- Resource signals: GPU memory used spikes aligned with batched embed flushes; KV cache eviction rate increased by ~3.2x versus baseline. PCIe swap counters rose modestly (not full OOM) but there were short-lived host-level swaps for the embedding kernel under heavy batch flush.

Hypothesis chain (why p99 explodes):
1) Embedding batches (when they flush) allocate intermediate tensors and force host-side copies when contiguous allocations can't be satisfied due to large pinned KV cache blocks.
2) The runtime's soft-priority preemption moves small background lanes off GPU; but reactivation and reallocation cause stalls while kernels rebind memory -> long tail.
3) Large gen contexts keep KV cache entries pinned for longer, increasing fragmentation and reducing contiguous free regions.
4) Result: occasional blocking for tens to hundreds of ms while memory relocations happen -> p99.

Quick experiments I ran to validate hypotheses (notes and outcomes):
- Disable embedding batching (batch_size=1): p99 for gen drops from 1.8s -> 760ms. Embed latency median increases ~2x but no second mode. Interpretation: batching was the trigger for allocation spikes.
- Increase batching window to 25ms (bigger, fewer flushes): p99 for gen increases slightly vs baseline but fewer distinct spikes; embedding jitter higher. Suggests batching timing affects synchrony of allocation pressure.
- Force KV cache eviction policy to LRU-prioritize-gen (prefer evicting embeddings): p99 drops to ~600ms but embedding failures (recomputations) increase CPU work. Tradeoff: tail improves, throughput cost for embeds.
- Try stricter preemption (immediate preempt background): reduced p99 to ~500ms but caused thrash on small background jobs (embed QPS dropped 18%).

Actionable quick items (short-term):
- Safety net: add a targeted circuit breaker that throttles embed batching when gen queue depth > X. Implementation: per-gpu token-budget threshold. (Owner: Lina)
- Micro-optimization: try a defragmentation pass for GPU memory between large context generations in low-util windows. Risk: CPU overhead. (Owner: Marco)
- Telemetry: add per-request memory-alloc delta metric + mark requests that triggered kernel rebinds. Need an event flag in runtime. (Owner: me)

Longer-term ideas (researchy):
- Separate memory pools by workload class (pinned KV pages vs transient embed scratch). Essentially partition address space to reduce fragmentation interplay.
- Promote asynchronous embed offload when gen concurrency > threshold: move embedding kernels to a dedicated inference accelerator or float to CPU offload for batched embeds.
- Workload-aware batching: dynamically disable/enable embedding batching per host based on gen KV pressure and predicted context sizes.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Is the fragmentation pattern reproducible across A100 <-> H100? I have only tested A100. Need cross-hardware run.
- Does quantization mode (int8 vs q4) alter allocation shapes enough to avoid fragmentation? Quick local test: int8 gen seemed slightly friendlier (p99 ~ -12%) but need thorough sweep.
- How often do these mixes occur in real tenant traffic? Need sample from prod: run a 2-hour sliding window classification of request classes (embed vs gen) and correlate with tail events (JIRA-RT-3172).

Experiment log snippets (for later copy to perf infra):
- run_id: poly-2026-02-24-01, cfg: mix=30/70, ctx=2048, embed_batch=8, clients=poisson-mean-85. Observed: gen_p99=1.8s, kv_eviction_rate=3.2x, swap_events=6.
- run_id: poly-2026-02-24-02, cfg: embed_batch=1 (other params same). Observed: gen_p99=760ms, embed_median=85ms, swap_events=1.

Draft runbook blurb (for ops):
- If tenant reports tail > 1s and we see concurrent embedding bursts: temporarily throttle embedding batching (API-level soft cap) and re-route heavy embedding traffic to hosts dedicated for batch inference. If no dedicated hosts available, escalate to on-call SRE to consider temporary tenant isolation.

Next immediate experiments I want to run (ordered):
1) Cross-HW replicate A100 -> H100; 3 runs each mix ratio.
2) Probe quantization variants (fp16 / int8 / q4) with ctx=4096 to maximize KV pressure.
3) Sweep embed batch sizes 1..64 and measure alloc delta histograms (need new metric).
4) Implement flagged kernel-rebind event trace and rerun the 30/70 baseline to correlate exact stacks.

TODOs:
- [ ] Add alloc-delta telemetry (me)
- [ ] Open GH perf PR to gate embed batch when gen queue > threshold (Lina)
- [ ] Cross-hardware runs and post results to JIRA-RT-3172 (Marco)

Final quick take: polyload is real and shows that batching heuristics tuned for homogeneous traffic break down in mixed workload scenarios. The fastest mitigation is conservative embed batching during high-gen pressure and better telemetry to identify kernel rebind events. Longer-term is memory partitioning or workload-aware scheduling.

Scratchpad ends — save and move key data to a proper experiment spreadsheet if we decide to pursue gate change.
